transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I... I suppose I'm here because of the voices. Well, not voices, exactly. It's... it's people talking. 

I keep hearing them. Usually the board members, or some of the staff. They talk about me through the conference room walls. Or... or sometimes it comes from my phone, even when it's completely powered down. They just keep saying I'm ruining the company. It's so clear, I actually answer them out loud before I realize... before I realize no one else in the room heard it.
Have you ever had any other experiences where you believed something was happening or true that others don't seem to notice or agree with?
I... no. I don't think so. Just the talking. I don't really know what else you mean.
Do you believe that certain people are specifically targeting you or plotting against you in some way?
I... no. Not really. I just... I just hear what they're saying. I don't think there's a plot. They're just talking.
Have you ever believed something to be true that others say isn't, such as thinking someone is following you, watching you, or that you have special powers or importance that others don't recognize?
No... nothing like that. I don't... I'm just a normal person. No special powers or anything. And nobody's following me. I just... I just hear them talking. That's all.
Have there been times when you believed something strongly, like something was definitely going to happen or that someone definitely meant something, but it turned out not to be true?
I... no. Not really. I don't make things up in my head. I usually know what's going on. I told you, it's... it's just the talking. Nothing else.
Do you ever feel like the thoughts or things you hear are being placed inside your mind by someone else, or that they don't belong to you?
No. I... my thoughts are my own. Nobody is putting things in my head. It's just... like I keep saying, I just hear them talking. That's it.
Have you ever had beliefs or ideas that others find unusual or hard to understand, even if you're sure they're true?
No. I... I don't know what you mean by that. I just... I go to work, I come home. People understand me fine. It's just the voices. That's all there is to it.
Have you ever had any ideas or beliefs that other people might find strange or unusual, even if they don't seem odd to you?
I think you just asked me that. Like I said... no. I don't have strange ideas. I just try to do my job and get through the day. I don't know why we keep going over this. It's just the voices.
Have you ever had any other thoughts or beliefs that you know are unusual but you still feel certain about, even if you haven't mentioned them yet?

I... I really don't understand why you keep asking me the exact same thing. Are you not listening to me? 

No. There's nothing else. Just what I already told you. I don't have anything else to add to that.
Have you ever seen things or felt sensations that others don't seem to notice, like seeing someone who isn't there or feeling something touching you when nothing is?

No. I don't... I don't see things that aren't there. And nobody is touching me. 

I told you, it's just the voices. That's it.

Have you ever had any beliefs or suspicions that others might not share, such as thinking someone has placed devices in your home, or that you are receiving special messages through TV or radio, for example?

Look... I feel like we are just going in circles now. 

No. No devices. No secret messages on the TV. I don't... I really don't know what else to say to you at this point. I just hear the voices. That's all.
Have you ever had any beliefs or ideas that you strongly held to be true, even when others gave you clear evidence that they were not true?

I... no. I don't. 

I really don't know how many different ways I can say it. I don't have any strange beliefs or... whatever it is you're looking for. I'm not making things up. Just... just what I already told you. That's it.

Have you ever believed something very strongly, even when there was clear proof it wasn't true, such as thinking something was definitely going to happen or that someone meant something specific, even if it turned out not to be the case?

I... didn't you just ask me that? 

No. I don't. I really don't have anything else to add to that. I don't know why you keep asking me the exact same thing.
Have you ever believed something very strongly that turned out not to be true, even if there was no voice or anyone telling you that it was true?

I... I don't know what you want me to say. 

I just said no. I don't... I don't have anything like that. I really don't understand why we're still on this.

Have you ever had any strong beliefs or ideas that turned out not to be true, even when there was clear evidence against them, such as thinking something was definitely going to happen or that someone meant something specific?

I... I feel like you're not listening to me. 

I've already answered this. The answer is still no. I don't have anything else to tell you about this. Can we please just move on?

I... I'm done answering this. 

You keep asking the same thing over and over. I told you no. I don't have anything else to say about it.

I don't... I really don't know what else you want from me. I've said no every single time you've asked. I am not answering this again.
Have you ever seen something that others say isn’t there, like a person, object, or image, even for a brief moment?
No. I haven't.

Have you ever been absolutely sure something was true, even when others showed you proof that it wasn’t, like thinking something was definitely going to happen or that someone meant something specific, even if it turned out not to be the case?
I... you just asked me that. I already told you no. I'm not going to keep repeating myself.

Have you ever had a strong belief or idea that you were absolutely sure was true, but others insisted it wasn’t, such as thinking something was going to happen, or that someone meant something specific, even if it turned out not to be true?

inference_history.note: The patient reports auditory hallucinations (hearing people talk about them through walls and from a powered-off phone) without clear delusions or other psychotic features. This rules out primarily mood disorders (F31, F32, F33, F34) and isolates psychotic-type disorders (F20, F22, F23). Schizophrenia (F20) and related disorders remain possible, as do delusional disorders (F22) and acute psychotic episodes (F23).

The patient consistently denied any delusional beliefs, special powers, or other unusual perceptions beyond auditory experiences (e.g., hearing people talk). No evidence of bizarre delusions, thought insertion, or other Schneiderian first-rank symptoms, which makes schizophrenia (F20.0, F20.1) and acute and transient psychotic disorders (F23.0, F23.1, F23.2, F23.8, F23.9) less likely. The presentation is more consistent with a delusional disorder or a persistent delusional-like experience that does not yet meet full criteria for schizophrenia.
